diet.name: Phase 1
diet.strategy: Starve pathogens, support liver detox, fuel gut repair.

items.name: Eggs (pasture-raised)
items.why: Complete amino acid profile, choline for liver.

items.name: Ground beef (grass-fed)
items.why: Iron, B12, zinc, saturated fat.

items.name: Beef/chicken bone broth
items.why: Liquid gut repair: glycine, proline, glutamine.

items.name: Chicken thighs (organic)
items.why: Fattier than breast = better nutrient absorption. Cheaper too.

items.name: Wild-caught salmon
items.why: Omega-3 anti-inflammatory + vitamin D.

items.name: Sardines (canned in olive oil)
items.why: Omega-3, calcium, virtually no mercury. Underrated powerhouse.

items.name: Broccoli, cauliflower, Brussels sprouts
items.why: Cruciferous = liver detox support (Phase II pathways).

items.name: Spinach, kale (sautéed)
items.why: Folate, magnesium, iron. Cooking reduces oxalates that can stress kidneys during kidney cleanse weeks.

items.name: Garlic & onions
items.why: Natural antimicrobials + prebiotic fiber. Allicin in garlic disrupts biofilms — supports what nattokinase + berberine are doing.

items.name: Zucchini & summer squash
items.why: Gentle on the gut, easy to digest, good vehicle for fats.

items.name: Celery
items.why: Natural electrolytes (sodium/potassium), anti-inflammatory apigenin. Great with guac.

items.name: Ginger root (fresh)
items.why: Anti-nausea (helpful during die-off), anti-inflammatory, supports digestion.

items.name: Sweet potatoes & butternut squash
items.why: Complex carbs that don't feed pathogens. Vitamin A for mucosal membranes.

items.name: Beef tallow (grass-fed)
items.why: Heat-stable cooking fat, rich in fat-soluble vitamins. Perfect for roasting and searing.

items.name: Avocados
items.why: Potassium, fiber, monounsaturated fat. Mash into guac or slice onto anything.

items.name: Extra virgin olive oil
items.why: Anti-inflammatory polyphenols. Use for finishing/dressings — don't high-heat cook with it.

items.name: Grass-fed butter / ghee
items.why: Ghee if dairy-sensitive.

groups.category: Fruits (treat as condiment, not food group)

items.name: Blueberries, raspberries, blackberries
items.why: Lowest sugar, highest antioxidant. A handful at the END of a meal, not alone.

items.name: Lemons & limes
items.why: Nearly zero sugar. Squeeze on meat, fish, water. Supports liver + digestion.

items.name: Green apple (Granny Smith)
items.why: Lower sugar than other apples. Pectin acts as a mild natural binder.

items.name: White rice
items.why: Easier on damaged gut than brown. Provides energy for detox without feeding pathogens significantly.

items.name: Sauerkraut (raw, refrigerated)
items.why: Live probiotics + prebiotic fiber. Just 1–2 tbsp with a meal — don't overdo during active killing.

items.name: Herbs: rosemary, thyme, oregano
items.why: All mildly antimicrobial. Season generously — food as medicine.

items.name: Apple cider vinegar (raw)
items.why: Supports stomach acid production. 1 tbsp in water before breaking fast can aid digestion.

items.name: Coconut aminos
items.why: Soy sauce replacement. No soy, no gluten, lower sodium.

diet.name: Phase 2
diet.strategy: Heavy killing is done. Now repair gut lining, rebuild microbiome diversity, increase fermented foods gradually, and maintain the anti-pathogen dietary framework. You can start loosening slightly but sugar remains restricted.

items.name: Kefir (plain, full-fat)
items.why: More probiotic diversity than yogurt. Start with 1/4 cup and build up.

items.name: Goat/sheep dairy
items.why: A2 casein is less inflammatory than cow A1. Goat yogurt, sheep feta — good options.

items.name: Increased sauerkraut & kimchi
items.why: Scale up to 2–4 tbsp per meal.

items.name: Prebiotic foods (after Wk 5+)
items.why: Cooked onions, garlic, asparagus, leeks, slightly green bananas.

items.name: Wider vegetable variety
items.why: Artichokes, asparagus, fennel, beets.

diet.name: Phase 3
diet.strategy: Gut is repaired, pathogens cleared. Now optimize for cellular energy, hormonal balance, and longevity. Diet expands significantly but stays whole-food based. Anti-inflammatory emphasis shifts to pro-metabolic.

items.name: Full dairy reintroduction (if tolerated)
items.why: Grass-fed yogurt, kefir, cottage cheese, aged cheeses freely.

items.name: Wider fish variety
items.why: Mackerel, trout, cod, shrimp. Omega-3 diversity supports cellular optimization.

items.name: Organ meats
items.why: Heart, liver, kidney — nutrient density supports the Rho Stack's cellular goals.

items.name: Raw honey (moderate)
items.why: Antimicrobial, prebiotic. Up to 1 tbsp/day is reasonable now.

items.name: Wider fruit access
items.why: Pears, peaches, apples of any variety. Still moderate tropical fruits.

items.name: Legumes more freely
items.why: Lentils, chickpeas, black beans. Good fiber + prebiotic diversity for established microbiome.

items.name: Whole, unprocessed foods — always
items.why: If it has a label with ingredients you can't pronounce, skip it.

items.name: High-quality proteins daily
items.why: Eggs, grass-fed beef, wild fish, organ meats. The carnivore instinct serves you well — keep it.

items.name: Abundant vegetables
items.why: Variety and color. Rotate through seasons. Cruciferous stays important for liver + estrogen metabolism.

items.name: Healthy fats at every meal
items.why: Tallow, butter, ghee, olive oil, avocado, coconut oil. Fat-soluble vitamin absorption is permanent.

items.name: Fermented foods daily
items.why: Sauerkraut, kimchi, kefir, yogurt.

spacing.detail: Activated charcoal, zeolite, clay and similar bind what is in the gut — including food, supplements and medication. Two hours clear on either side, or they bind the thing you meant to absorb.
Vitamins A, D, E and K, and anything oil-based, absorb with a meal that contains fat. On an empty stomach much of it passes through.

spacing.rule: Some things are hard on an empty stomach
spacing.detail: Anything that reliably causes nausea taken fasted is telling you something. With food is not a weaker dose, it is a tolerated one.
Calcium, magnesium, zinc and iron all use overlapping transport. Split them across the day rather than stacking them in one handful.

spacing.rule: Stimulating in the morning, settling at night
spacing.detail: Anything that lifts energy belongs early; anything that downshifts belongs late. The same substance at the wrong end of the day works against you.

spacing.rule: Space it out, then check it
spacing.detail: When two things must not meet, two hours is the usual working answer — but the label, the pharmacist and the prescriber outrank a rule of thumb, every time.
